title: mark knopfler - song for sonny liston
content: (from his new solo EP - The Trawlerman's Song) No need to introduce the Dire Straits mainman, who can forget "Money for Nothing" or the "Walk of Life" (or countless other non-commercial greats) , this is a b-side song from his new EP. It's got a perfect distorted blues guitar, and a great vibe, and his voice is still very powerful and unique. extra : elevatormoods.com - short movies taken in elevators, interesting, read the elefesto :) nice presentation

title: amy denio - birthing chair blues
content:
It's taken me apx. 20 years of conscious music listening to hear a song from Amy Denio, and what's ironic is it's the opener of her debut solo album from 1991. This song is an instant classic for me, her voice and songwriting skills are terrific, and her sound is a very unique mixture of soo many different elements. Well then how on earth did it take me so long to get a hold of this lady's album?!.
  • She is a composer, singer, multi-instrumentalist, audio engineer, international collaborator, and founder of her own record label & publishing company, Spoot Music. Her main instruments are voice, accordion, saxophones, clarinet, electric guitar, and bass.
  • She has 32 CD releases, and appears on several dozen audio compilations world-wide.
  • In 1997 she received the Bessie Award (NYC) for her soundtrack to David Dorfman Dance's "Sky Down,
  • Her soundtrack for "Pangaea's Brood" by Thomas Edward helped the film win "Best Animated Film" at the 1997 New York Underground Film Festival.
  • She has taught workshops on improvisation and composition in Italy, Austria, Belgium and in the US.
    • Avid listeners should definitely notice the resemblance of the "hello, hello" part to the Nirvana classic "Smells like Teen Spirit", which reminded me of a bootleg i had. So check out this song from Nirvana, apparently from one of their last shows, in Rome from 1994, (well, maybe not so rare, but who am I to know), and also these audio snippets of Kurt Cobain talking to the crowd from the same concert here and here..

title: architecture in helsinki - do the whirlwind
content: (from their new album "In case we die".) I felt kinda let down when i found out that Architecture in Helsinki wasn't from Helsinki, i don't know why, but they're from Australia and maybe i should have been happier because i never thought this kind of music would come out of Australia. This may be a soundtrack to a very surreal and fun world, so if you're a serious type of guy, you probably wouldn't get it at all, hehe.. title: korsakow - sweat
content: (taken from his new album Ears on Komfort Music) Korsakow is Dub Taylor. Sweat is an uptempo deep house tune on his new album, with retro synths and percussions similar to the classic Metro Area album with some German deep-house flavor. He has a new album out on Komfort Music, and it's minimal deep house in the vein of Dessous and Pokerflat labels. Louie Austen also makes a guest appearance on the album on the song Open up your heart. EXTRA : Listen to some Louie Austen tracks from 2003's Easy Love album on Kitty-Yo here. That was one hell of an album..

title: minotaur shock - somebody once told me..
content: (taken from his Maritime album on 4AD) Minotaur Shock is David Edwards, from Bristol, and he has just released an outstanding 2nd album on 4AD released last month. . The album is labeled as folktronica by critics although he's not happy with the generalisation (folktronica?!) . It's a melodic album with a subtle dose of accoustic instruments (mostly brasses) and yes, cheerful folkish melodies i should say. However the amalgamation of electronic bits and the acoustic bits are so perfect it's almost natural. This is not a gimmick album, his humour and worldview is branded in his music for sure. This kind of music really grew on me for the last months (folktronica?!!), and this album is a milestone album that i should rate every new album i listen in this genre hereafter. you can check out his microsite on 4AD records, until his official site is back up. Here is an interview done with him in May and here is a review from Milk Factory. EXTRA : a french mp3blog article on folktronica, has downloads of Khonnor and Tunng. another mp3blog article , for samples of Pastacas from Kohvi records, his album Tsaca Tsap has been on my playlist for a few months, and it's a surprisingly good, Estonian electronic pop album. He really deserves attention! :) ANOTHER EXTRA : ok i just couldn't decide which song to post, so i'm posting another one and i repeat, this album is the new sensation :)

title: plantlife - when she smiles she lights the sky
content: (taken from their luv 4 the world EP) it seems i'm a bit late to jump on Plantlife, i just heard this EP, and i realized that they've won a best album award from Gilles Peterson last year, and countless comments from people like Pharell, Def Mos, Xzibit, and no it's not a hiphop album. It's some unique mixture of a soulful downbeat jazz disco hiphop hybrid, kind of stuff that you'd like to hear from Master Gilles. The LA band has already begun touring with Gilles Peterson and been covered everywhere intensively. This EP has some King Britt remixes, but i preferred to post the original. EXTRA : download plantlife - appreciate on their own record label's page, and then go check out the comments @ the official site here or check out Worldwide 2004 best album/track winners here

title: jamie lidell - what's the use
content: well, his new album is really the new sensation!.. I had always known about him, but categorized him in the inaccessible technoish music folder in my head, (a la cristian vogel, marcin czubala .. dunno why). Last year everybody was talking about his hyper-live show, including Isolee (he was blown away by his live show), and now his new album Multiply is out, and it sure is accessible. It's a soulful groovy laidback motown electronica hybrid. Reminded me a bit of Burnt Friedman & The Nu-dub Players. I'm surprised, i'm really surprised. The song "multiply" has been automatic repetition in my head for the last 2 weeks, but i'm gonna promo another one, (you can find "multiply" on fluxblog, if the links haven't died, yet, and you *should* it's a mega-hit in my opinion.) ok best of all, i found the link to his live show video (it wasn't that hard!) here at warp's site.. if you have the smallest idea to do a liveshow you should check this out, because the bar has been raised now! :) you can read a gig review here , and an interview with the man here

title: 2 netlabel recommendations
content: This time i've got 2 recent netlabel releases under my belt Muhr - La chute du romantisme en ball EP on Miasmah : solid ambient / folkish debut, from Canadian Muhr, it's got some beats here and there but mostly ambient with a little bit of ethnic twist. Bacanal Intruder - Herramientas Para Abrir Un Libro EP on Test Tube : very nice folktronica album (i wonder is it a legal genre now :) ) from Spain, short songs based on guitars and other accoustic instruments and some electronic beats. This is a delicate recording, i am pretty sure you will be satisfied with this rather short (16 minutes) ride, and come back to it for more.

title: deerhoof the great!
content:
deerhoof, is teh funniest!! > i've read so many interviews and i've never read a serious answer, take a look @ this interview from pitchfork ;

"Do you want to say anything about Milk Man's song writing process? Things you did differently than in Reveille, and were there any specific reasons or conscious decisions to avoid things?"

Deerhoof: The process used to be that I would brush my teeth, go to bed, and in that world of twilight consciousness, start hearing melodies and things. On Milk Man the process was different, because I realized that it's also important to floss.

see?

deerhoof, is also the coolest > because they release most of their stuff free on the net, and doesn't sue you.. for example here , you can get 23 deerhoof songs. (saving my ass from ripping 2 mp3 and uploading to my server at the same time) Check out my pal foot foot to get some first impressions. i'm pretty sure you would like more interviews, and more songs, so check out the song "Come see the Duck" on Orbis Quintus while the link still lasts. And here is their official site

title: Slope ft. Capital A - Komputa Groove
content: (12" single from their Komputa Groove LP on Sonar Kollektiv) Well if the Recloose track wasn't enough for you, here's another brilliant song, this time from Sonar Kollektiv's 2-piece Slope. Very innovative song, you would immediately feel these boys have established their own style. Cheerful mood again, in 2/4 shuffle beat with filtered keys, and pseudo-strings. If you are amazed by the first 1:30 of this song just wait till Capital A begins his rap-song hybrid. The flipside of the vinyl is also an incredibly eclectic boogie monster with Ovasoul 7's vocals. I'm dying to get my hands on the full LP release, which is as big as the Metro Area's self titled album release in 2002. You can listen to excerpts from all the songs on the LP here on Sonar Kollektiv's site. (respect!)

title: Recloose - Dust
content: (from his Dust 12" on Peacefrog) After a few days of rest without a computer, here are some new selections that has cheered me up during that time. This is an incredible toon (note my devious mixture of tune and cartoon) with a jazzy organ and horn stabs, a groovy bassline and witty lyrics, it's almost impossible to resist the cartoonish mood of this song, don't be mistaken this is not jazz but a very eclectic mixture, it's a perfect dancy beginner for a sunny day and i'm not sure if you can resist the urge to repeat this song for at least 3 times in a row. Alright my words don't do it enough justice i know, but this goes straight to the "top 2005 songs" bin. This 12" includes a 7 minute main mix, which is the real deal. The vocals are by Joe Dukie from Fat Freddy's Drop which is a 7 piece dub band from New Zealand. EXTRA : you can listen to a live recording by Recloose @ milkaudio (Real Media)

title: rednose distrikt - bling bling
content: from their denk ik EP on KBR) is this minimal hiphop? maybe there's not enough rapping, but it surely is full of bling blings!. this is some swingin' downtempo/hiphop with a nice subbass tone, and a catchy vocal line going "no more bling bling".. the EP consists of newer stuff after kid sublime left the band, kid sublime has also released a new solo album recently in May as well..

title: netlabel fellas
content: sorry for no posts for some time, it's intolerably hot here :) i had some netlabel stuff i wanted to mention in the past days, but i couldn't find the time to do it.. (doesn't time seem to fly by?) the first one is an ep by starfros.ch collective on RealAudio , it's mellow, guitar based pop with vocals, an answer to US urban pop music from switzerland. it kinda sounds like morcheeba meets IDM to me in some parts. First track to preview should be #2 don't stop if you like dreamy hiphopish sounds, or #4 star guitar if you wanna hear some great jazzy dnb. . but you should go and download the full EP here. #2 is Stephane Obadia as Rob Steady on 12 Rec apparently he is a cool dude from France (but living in Stockholm as i interpreted from the website . - ha! ) He has been involved with different media all the while and this album is an interesting cut-up experience that intrigued me a lot at the first listen. After some listens, yes, this album has some brilliant moments. His beats are incredible and the album is very humorous, i am really looking forward to more releases from him. It is probably far out there for many listeners, but if shifting time signatures, sweet childish melodies, very complex arrangements or oddity is your thing, and you like music that changes every 30 seconds like hyperactive kids (which i love!) or ends abruptly you'll love this album!!!

title: The words of an oak!
content: well after all the live 8 shows, you're probably having a music overload, and wanna rest your head without any music.. Think again!! you can't live without music, you know that.. Well once you come to terms with that, here's mix.no#4 from our friend hecanjog. Let me get it straight, it's been a long time since I stopped thinking djing is cool, but of course once in a while stuff like this happens to change my mind. These mixes span across many genres, from accoustic stuff to short passages of speech or noise, to electronic stuff, to avantgarde jazz to neo-folk and indie, it's almost like changing channels on the radio, albeit the random factor! and he also has an exquisite music taste of hard to come-by tracks most of the stuff that i'm sure you'd fall in love with at least 2 every mix, (at least!) Stuff from people like C.Penrose, Jandek, Kemialliset Ystävät, Murcof, Lau Nau, Lightning Bolt, Akira Rabelais and more, I hope I managed to get your attention by now so just go to this page and get all the 4 mixes while it lasts!

title: Dub Guerilla - The Curse
content: (from their self-titled 2005 album) The opener of this incredible dub-ska-jazz hybrid album, is a very special song. I don't know why but it reminds me of pirates, and conjures some yellow screens of the Caribbean (or maybe Arabian? - i don't know) in my head. Dub Guerilla is a 14-piece band, featuring none other than the gifted German trombonist Dr. Ring Ding (he is from Germany, and he's played with The Toasters, and The Skatalites - that's incredible in itself) and Jazzkantine's Tom Bennecke. Well ok even if you have never heard of them, or even if you don't like dub, give it a try because this album is not another boring dub album, and this song is just the perfect teaser.. Download it here Listen to samples of the full album here and buy it.

title: Beans - Down by Law
content: (from 2004's down by law EP) well look at this man, how can you resist him now? He's one of the elitest MCs and the talk of the town nowadays. title: Rocky Marsiano
content:
Tags: hiphop , lisbon , jazzy , boxing , heavyweight
...aaaaaaaand here comes the world heavy weight boxing champion! Rocky Marsiano aka D-Mars. Well, I wanted to write extensively about him, but every link to him or his excellent album "The Pyramid Sessions" on Loop Recordings, (even his artist info on Loop) is in Portuguese. But thanks to the Babelfish translation service i've got some clues ! :) D-Mars is a hiphop producer from Lisbon, and his style fuses old 50's jazz styles into blunted instrumental hiphop beats, you know like early DJ Cam stuff, with vibrophone solos, occasional scratching, incredible jazzy melodies, moody pads, the swing bass, the guitar solos.. It really made me go to the late 40s 50s boxing scene, with cuban cigars in my hand, listening to jazz in a classy jazz venue while eating my lobster after my boxer has won the title fight.. well, ok call me a day dreamer, but listen to Rocky Marsiano.. Download jam of the month here Download round the block session go and checkout samples from the rest of the album read an interview (in portuguese) read about the original Rocky Marciano (the only Heavyweight champion to go undefeated)

title: Ammon Contact - Naeem
content: (from their 2005 CD New Birth) well we all have learnt by now that not all music should be party music, or phenomenal in success to be labelled good. We love those simple, moody, cinematique music that goes seemingly unnoticed, but your brain memorizes every beat or melody as a background process.. ammoncontact's latest offering on the legendary ninja tune has 9 tracks (LP has 10) of this calibre, a subtle mix of downtempo (with subtle hints of 70s soul and funk) electronica and instrumental hiphop, from the Los Angeles duo. It's a head-bopper for sure!.. this song has an incredible guitar lick (that gets stuck on your head instantly!) going on a nice bassline , and it will make you happy for 2.19 minutes :) Download Ammon Contact - Naeem Read a review of Ammon Contact - New Birth. Listen to more samples from the album (real audio).

title: Tiburon - Shake me
content: I don't know what you feel about this latest electro-house-acid breed that everybody's playing, maybe it's getting a little bit overplayed, but anyways, it's the first time i'm publishing an electro-house track, and it defines the standards :) This is Lance DeSardi with a new alias, on the US label Coma. It's not his usual style though if you know the lad, it's dark and electrifying, with a catchy vocal hook.. Download Tiburon - Shake me. Buy it here. There's also a netlabel i wanna mention, releasing mostly electro-house/tech-house. Peromusic, has just done their 8th release, by Sajad. It's standard tech-house with the electro feel, it's party music for the 2005! If you like this kind of grooves give the label a try. Download Sajad - Skyscraper EP.

title: Tangoterje - Can't help It
content: (from the "Can't help It" EP on G.A.M.M) Such a joy to have found this. I've been listening to this one for more than a month when i realized that I should get off my ass and share this definitive summer hit! (albeit in small circles) This is a cover (Hey, it's not a cheap commercial remix/bootleg to make money off an old hit, like most of the music industry does nowadays!)of Jacko's "Can't help it", and such a good one it is!. (produced by Stevie Wonder for him, cool!) Well MJ's singing was perfect in this era, the song was a hit, and the 70s disco strings and latin percussions added make this song shine. BTW Tangoterje is Todd Terje. and you would really regret it, if you pass this one. :) Download Tangoterje - I can't help it Buy the 12" here And also, i fucked up the Tiburon mp3 and posted an incomplete one. It's OK now, so you can safely download it below..

Pitchfork review of Isolee's We are Monster
The CD Sequencer by Matthew Falla - WOW, what a novel idea. The CD Sequencer is an innovative new concept for interactive CD packaging. You can use printed postcards to remix music and store your mixes or share them with friends. Draw on the cards to remix the tunes. If you are happy with a mix, you can remove the card and save it for later. The remix is "stored" on the card until the next time you insert it, when it immediately plays back. Kracfive - Iron Chef of Music battles - electronic music battles from Kracfive artists, all songs are available as mp3s.. artists include Kettel, Colongib, Khonnor and more.. also check out their monthly mp3 releases here

title: Bus featuring Earl 16 - Simple Way
content: (from the 2004 compilation named Hitek by Meteosound) I wouldn't hide I'm a big fan of ~Scape records, the sound of Pole and Jan Jelinek, the mature and refined sound of Berlin. I remember when I first listened to the first Farben EPs by Jelinek in 2000 and the Loop-Finding-Jazz-Records album next year, they have been truly inspirational and really opened my ears (and yours maybe?) to all kinds of beautiful music. The people behind Bus is Daniel Meteo and Tom Thiel, two musicians from Berlin and their dub inspired electronic music surely has the Berlin aesthetics written all over it. This song is from an 2004 compilation on Meteosound, their own label. Sweet vocals by Leftfield's Earl 16. Definitely a must. Download Bus featuring Earl 16 - Simple Ways. Check out an interview with Pole. Read the Loop-finding-Jazz-Records review on Pitchfork (A whoppin' 9.3)

title: Matthew Herbert and a little break
content: (from his Plat du Jour album on his own Accidental records) Well, the boss is back for a new album. You know you can never go wrong with Mr. Herbert, he is constantly experimenting, yet always sounding accessible and musical. This song is off his new album, it features Dani on vocals, and it's a satire about modern day celebrities (Go David! Victoria! Go Beyonce Go Beyonce!). Cheerful downtempo electronica with little bleeps and melodies going in the background, and with beautiful vocalwork from Dani.. And with that we conclude the intro to undomondo :) , I'll be away on vacation till the 2nd week of August, so no new posts till we make the greatest comeback known in the universe! title: Devendra Banhart  - Chinese Children
content: Well well, the king is back! and what better way to get back from vacation and start off with him. A quick info if you have been away on a space trip, stuck with your old cds for the last 1-2 years, there's a new music genre labelled the "New Weird America", it's a retake on psychedelic folk music of the 60s and 70s. (You're lucky if you have been on an acid trip for the last 30 years, you'll think nothing has changed!) Anyways, Devendra is one of the most accessible (so long Beatles!) versatile and sincere songwriter I've ever listened to, his mind seems to be sparkling with ideas for little folk-pop songs, and his voice!! You've got to hear his gentle voice. Here's a silly pop song that has a very oldschool bluesy feeling, and funny lyrics like "If i lived in China, I'd have some Chinese children, but out of my toes my little black baby grows, and that's my fact!" Get it! title: Bloc Party - The pioneers (Bloc party vs Mystery jets)
content: The only downside to this years brilliant Bloc Party debut album was that it was too generic, it was like all the indie rock groups you've heard before, albeit perfected. This little tune here got covered by the Mystery Jets and it has a great sloppy drum/percussion beat going on now, the vocals are slower and laid back, and the song is not indie rock anymore, but soft and laid back indie dance ? This is a great cover, which is IMHO better than the original, but it's not valid to say this, because the songs are totally different. Download Bloc Party - The pioneers (Bloc party vs Mystery jets) Download 3 Bloc Party tracks live @ XFM (via Mr. Red Penguin's mp3blog)

title: Jeff Recordings - Crippled Dick Hot Wax
content: Today i have two special world music songs from a rare and unique compilation on the CDHW label. Both of these songs have been engineered by Gerhard "Jeff" Nieckau, a German sound-engineer, who, in order to explore new music during the 70s set out on a journey to Peru and Trinidad & Tobago, and is also known to be the engineer behind Bossa 70 from Peru. What a wonderful idea for a compilation!. Ranging from calypso to afrobeat and more, the tracks sound raw and they still have the marks of history on them. Should you like these two tracks below, i'm 100% positive you'd be delighted to have this album permanently for your archive. :) And you should definitely read about Mr. Jeff Nieckau (born 1923), one of the pioneers of sound engineering and open-mindedness (something we still need in music biz!) Download Lancelot Layne - Yo tink it sorf? Download Gay Flamingoes Steelband - Caterpilla (Lou Donaldson cover) Timeline of Trends in Music from Wikipedia. (Nice read! - a sidenote; 1971 - Lancelot Layne's "Blown Away" is the beginning of rapso music.)

title: VVV - I got wheels, I got nails
content: (from their 2005 album on Mego) A claustrophobic track on this dark and cloudy Istanbul afternoon (it should have been better it's august for God's sake!) VVV is a collaboration of well-known musicians; Mika Vainio and Ilpo Vaisanen from Pan sonic, the Finnish kings of noise and Alan Vega, the infamous frontman of Suicide. And as you expected, the release is as dark and gloomy it gets. Alan Vega is enchanting as a vocalist,(although Stylus Mag says he's getting old) his strange lyrics and growls are in the front, while the Pan sonic crew set the catatonic mood of the songs. Stylewise, I really think this album is similar to the AGF/Delay release "Explode Baby". Slow minimal and noisy, with a strange groove behind all songs. However this album is as dark and creepy as a David Lynch movie. So beware! Download VVV - I got wheels, I got nails

title: Coolest band names!
content:
I really think there's a correlation between the coolness of a band name and the coolness of the music they do.. I've been intrigued many times by the name of a band or person, and tried to find out if they sound as good as their name.. And most of the time, i've not been disappointed. Yesterday I saw a band named "Stop coming to my house Prom Queen" and I thought "Hey why don't I make a post about weird&cool band names", and ended up doing this. So feel free to comment if you wanna add some weird named and cool band/groups, in fact PLEASE do so. :) Here is the first 10 randomly ordered..

title: isn't it bad
content:
well, today was the first time i had the direct linking terror happen to me. i came home and i checked the logs for the blog for newcomers, and stats. i saw a blog linking to me and i had terrific download and view stats for edgar allen floe.. then upon some further investigation, i noticed that there were no actual users, but the blog that linked to me, had embedded all the content (not only mine) in the page directly, without mentioning the link to undomondo anywhere, thus slowly eating my bandwidth without giving me any new readers :/

the worst part is, that there are like 20 more songs on the front page, which begin to load automatically when you load the page, meaning you eat bandwidth whether you wanna listen to those tracks or not. 

a terrible bandwidth hog, a black hole i should say.. 

I think i'll go and pray to lord that i don't witness another direct linkage again.

title: aren't netlabels great?
content: Folks don't you think that netlabels are getting better day by day?. Netlabel fans are growing, music is getting better, new labels are being founded, artists are getting much more coverage, and it's not seen as a "low-quality alternative" to CD labels anymore.. (how can we forget the traditional vinyl or cd guy smirking netlabels and artists back then?) The releases below are the main cause of the above paragraph. 4 solid releases and all you've got to do to is to click the link and you can have it for free.. when was the last time someone gave you something this good for free? go ahead and support these artists! (and other netlabels too of course!) Jahtari 06 by Bo Marley : Great great vocal track from Bo Marley. Jahtari are fellow dub/reggaeheads, and this is their first vocal release. The dub version on side b is totally a hit, and one of the best digital dub tracks ever created since Basic Channel! Beat is Murder 01 by Yeah pretty boy : Beat is Murder is a new post-electronica label, with 2 releases, this is the first one from YPB. Glitchy electronic pop in the vein of Dat Politics. Pharmacom 01 by Calypso : Lounge music from Italy. Delicate downtempo acid jazz with vocals, similar to Koop. Stroem 08 by MichL Bridge : The last of the bunch is a release from the Swedish Stroem label. They have some great releases under their belt, and they really push the boundaries for fresh music . This is a unique release of 6 parts fading into each other, but you'd never know that if I didn't mention it, because MichL has created a special sonic journey with such complex arrangement and storytelling, it will put some noteworthy ambient-cinematique music artists to shame. I'm totally totally in love with this one.

title: Espen Horne - Ain't no Sunshine
content: (from his 2005 EP on Hi-Fi Terapi) Mr. Horne is a talented musicman from Bergen, Norway and this song is off his debut release on the yummy Norwegian label Hi-Fi Terapi. Espen is not a newcomer in the scene though, he has released many records on the ever-successful Stereo Deluxe label as Bobby Hughes and on the Tru Thoughts label as Kinny & Horne with Caitlin Simpson. This return to a local label, sees him doing a brilliant cover work of Bill Withers' Ain't no Sunshine (Ain't no sunshine when she's gone/It's not warm when she's away/Ain't no sunshine when she's gone/and she's always gone too long/Anytime she goes away). Chopped up beats, retro organs, and beautiful urban acidjazz interpretation by Kinny, takes the song to such a level, that we previously thought only Dani and Herbert could achieve. Up there with the Sonar Kollektiv and Compost releases, I'm sure Mr. Gilles Peterson is cranking it up everyday. :) Download Espen Horne - Ain't no Sunshine Download samples from other Hi-Fi Terapi artists (Norwegian Jazz & House) Buy Hi-Fi Terapi releases

title: General Electrics
content: Great EP on Compost by the French keyboardist Hervé Salters aka General Electrics. 4 original songs and 2 remixes on this one. The Compost website labels his music as Sunday Morning goodness and it really feels good to listen to these tracks on a sunday morning like this. The song Catch the Bus begins with a noisy synth and then mutates into a 70s spygroove , lounge track. Terms and Conditions remix by The Entity on the other end is a top-notch track. An excellent shuffle-beat recreates the song in German territory. Not the usual compost style, but if you like the AtomTM works on Rather Interesting or if you went to Sonar this year, you should like these tracks. :) Download Catch the Bus Download Terms and Conditions (The Entity Remix)

title: Flanger - Crime in the Pale Moonlight
content: (from their 2005 album Spirituals) Flanger has been an inspirational band for the last few years (although the name sux :P), thanks to the sheer brilliance of AtomTM and Bernd Friedman. Both have delivered exceptional releases on many labels (Ninja Tune, Rather Interesting, K7 etc.) and many names (Senor Coconut, Atom Heart, Burnt Friedman & The Nu Dub Players) and they continue to do so with this album. Firmly rooted in jazz, the music is a revisit to the melancholy of the oldtimes (1920's dixie), but the production methods and the sound is very fresh because of electronics. The music is so fitting as a last homage to the birth place of Jazz, New Orleans, and it feels pretty sad. Vocals here and there, it's jazzy easy listening music, but something very special from gifted musicians. and from the website : "This album is not about re-constructing endless virtuoso solos via mere knob-twiddling. With Spirituals, Flanger first of all want to explore and relive the emotional sides of this jazz-before-jazz, its moods and sentiments. As Friedman points out, the album may very well be seen as "the restoration of a lost sensibility". Download How long is the wrong way Download Crime in the Pale Moonlight Read an interview with Bernd Buy the album

title: Jamie Saft Trio - Shalmiel
content:
The first time I heard the name of Tzadik label, it's strange name intrigued me a lot. Later I figured out that, it was a figment of John Zorn's imagination, and from then on I listened to many Tzadik releases, and I am now confident that I like most of their releases (although some are non-listenable). This lil song here is not inaccessible at all, a modern Jewish jazz version by Zorn that opens the second book of the Masada project. Played beautifully by Jamie Saft on Piano, Greg Cohen (Masada, Ornette Coleman) on bass and Ben Perowsky (Uri Caine, John Scofield) on drums, the Tzadik label has been giving Jewish music a revamp through the last few years. I am hooked on these melancholic chords and cinematic melodies. This is avant jazz at its best (and most accessible :) )
Download Jamie Saft Trio - Shalmiel
Read about Tzadik on the I Love Music board for more freejazz and avantgarde music advices.

title: 1 Kilo of Black Bondage - Unleah
content:
Continuing the tradition of weird names, a few days ago I came across this European electronica band. There's a sensible explanation to the name though. 1K of BB is actually 3 musicians, Black Sifichi, Aka_Bondage and 2 kilos and more, hence the name. Unleah is a strange piece, it's not a song, it's more like storytelling with the help of music. The beginning is ambient with occasional creepy strings and water sounds. The music lumbers on with increasing tension, and around the first minute, samples off a possible movie dialogue enter, completing the haunting feeling. The texture work is great here and if you like Badalamenti stuff, you'll like it a lot. Ok, enough hints, you've got to listen to the full song, to find out how it resolves..
Buy the album directly from the Ronda Label
Download 1 Kilo of Black Bondage - Unleah

title: Netlabel releases for a rainy day
content: Hey, today I woke up with furious raining outside, and what better way to begin it with Tonepoem's Abandoned Amusements release on Earstroke netlabel. Dreamy, naive and mostly full of emotional melodies accompanying childhood memoirs, If you liked the Minotaur Shock album this year; you'd probably love to visit Mr. Rodinelli's imaginary landscape. Download Tonepoem - Abandoned Amusements Another suitable music for a rainy day should be, Miasmah 58 by Muhr: La chute du romantisme en ballades. Melancholic folk music, with delayed ambient guitar and string work reminiscent of many post-rock artists. It's romantic and depressing with a cinematic feeling. Soundtrack for a possible 15 minute short movie. Standout track for me is Le ciel sur les épaules, which is an ambient piece with strings and piano. Download Muhr - La chute du romantisme en ballades

title: Micatone - Where I am Part 2
content: Nice effort from this Berlin based Jazz-electronica fusion band. Vocalist Lisa Bassenge has a lovely voice and is quite powerful through all songs. Jazzy downtempo stuff with many different musical inspirations, in fact they surely are not any short of creative ideas, as songs are quite varied. I'm sure if you like bands like De-Phazz and Beady Belle, you'll be delighted with this nice solid LP. Where I am Part 2 is a slow one, perhaps the most electronic of them with reverbed bass and guitar backing Lisa's vocals. However as I said, there are many uptempo urban funk & jazz songs so if you want some more stuff to sample check out the links below. By the way it's out on Sonar Kollektiv and IMHO they are one of the best labels to blindly follow right now. Download Where I am Part 2 Sample more on Micatone's official page. title: free yourself from music within a day...
content:
..with the help of, who else, but mr. MichL Bridge, whom I've mentioned a few posts ago regarding his release on stroem. His last effort is a drony ambient piece on Luumu, which rotates around the concept of transformation. In each song he's taken one sample, and transformed it in time slowly. The music is very minimal, and it varies as if it's a natural transformation through time. That theme of slow change is IMO best visible on the opening track, where he's taken a marimba like sample and done some rhythmic variations to create an ambience. MichL has also added an accompanying text to the full archive (like the old demo scene text files, if you can recall), sharing his motives and mindset before and after the EP. I guess it's best to quote from his own text as a closing sentence; "i wanted the tracks to sound very simple and pure. they all should happen this special weekend to really proof that a kind of transformation is possible within that period of time. and to catch this feeling as true as possible. "
Get it here

title: Porn Sword Tobacco - Explains Freedom
content:
What a remarkable debut LP from Henrik Jonsson aka Porn Sword Tobacco!. and what a wonderful name to name your identity. An album recorded in a studio in the middle of a Swedish forest (probably with Sid Meiers' Pirates on the mind, or am I the only one who thinks the music or the name has a relation with pirates?), this album is emotionally laden like an Ulrich Schnauss album minus the weak drum programming of him *sorry* (as a matter of fact I now realize that both artists are on City Centre Offices) Old booze new friends, is a downtempo waltz, with ambient noises and an electric piano, a sad and emotional piece reminding me of a forgotten old radio show theme music. White Sneakers is a different story, relaxed and easygoing, it only has a bass and a monophonic synth playing some melodies.. I mean, come on it's pretty hard to create a piece this beautiful with this much elements. While the IDM world is getting bogged down with DSP FX and stuck with too much going on in the songs, this man comes up and says stop!, let's calm our heads a little bit! A must buy!
Read a review and buy the album Extra : how do you define bad musical taste? thread on ILX board.
Download Porn Sword Tobacco - Old Booze New Friends Download Porn Sword Tobacco - White Sneakers

title: broque #15 by even tuell
content:
I was checking around a little bit today and I came upon this nice release by Even Tuell, on the Broque netlabel which kindly published my debut EP a while ago. However I shall mention at first that this is in no way a favour review. It came my way from discoselector's neato blog, I thought the cover was very funny, and proceeded to check the music.. There once I got that off, I really found some of the stuff here very fresh for the minimal techno/house scene of late. Most of the German and Canadian innovators are repeating themselves, and the once cherished minimal house subgenre is full of mediocre releases now. This EP has a back to basics approach with raw percussive sounds, it is at times a bit dark and claustrophobic with some melodic phrases here and there, but to me the most important thing was the reminiscence of the old repetitive Detroit stuff or of early Studio 1. It's really roots rock minimal techno like the good old days.. (not the boring minimal party sounds of today!)
Go to Even Tuell - Power of Needles EP release page.
(I would link to the zip here, but it's a 80mb zip full of 4 different versions of each song , the ogg ,the vbr, etc. I mean, once I get the full zip, why would I want 4 different encoded versions of each song??. Other labels do this as well, so I wonder if it's a policy of archive.org? I don't know but I don't wanna download 80 megs, instead of a possible 31. )

title: Blend - What you sing is what you get
content:
Tags: athens , downtempo , jazz , funk , seventies
Sometimes you need a break from this problem ridden world.. A voice to assure you that things are getting better and you can now rest for a few minutes. This easy going song chanting "everything's gonna be alright" is just that!. When you listen to this song you'll be assured that it is going to be alright (provided it's a sunny day!) and you have an offbeat organ, a guitar, and some percussion.. Blend is the brainchild of George Mandas from Athens and is a sixpiece. if you like multicoloured and multiflavoured jazzfunky downtempo sounds, their new album is out on Sirius M41. Download Blend - What you sing is what you get Go to Blend Music Check out the netlabel Death to Spies which features Blend tracks among with other downtempo niceties from Papadog, Chix and the MLF.

title: Some new friends I made..
content: A few nice mp3blogs for your enjoyment.. * Schrikdraad from NL , from where you can find the links to download varied stuff like Ratatat, Bonobo, a Pink Floyd live from 1969, an Autechre bootleg, Neutral Milk Hotel, and Ini Kamoze?!? * The excellent xxxSurgeryxxx blog, which adds detailed electronic reviews and 50 minute mixes once in a while, featuring an excellent choice of tracks of minimal electronica, he's got 15 out, which includes tracks from Schwabinggrad Ballett, Akiyama/Kahn, Tujiko Noriko, Pan American and Porn Sword Tobacco.. What's more he archives his past shows, so don't you waste time because you never know when bandwidth's get exhausted. * Comfort Music is the blog of Comfort Radio featuring decent electronica, clash and trip-hop.. great relatively unknown finds (Luminescent Orchestrii, Finn. Chin Chin balanced with major players like Ladytron, Broken Social Scene and Goldfrapp) * And last but not least Aurgasm featuring the lovely Tin Hat Trio. If you like Mediterranean sounds with tango and accordeon, you're in for a treat.

title: Sunday Roundup
content: So many links so few time! I forgot to mention the new Sufjan Stevens on Gorilla vs Bear yesterday, go check it out while the link is still working, and also read this interview with him. (I thought Sufjan was a ethnic hippy personality like Devendra, i'm shocked!) Check out the In-Tune blog, for a guide in unsigned / netlabel electronica and reviews. I particularly liked the Photophob release on Earstroke. I was going to buy some stuff from Buy Olympia, a store i found out about yesterday, I was looking for some Deerhoof merchandise and saw lots of nice books and mags and stuff, however I had to pay 60% of the cost as shipping, therefore I cancelled all. We need teleportation now! I watched some excerpts from a concert in Turkey yesterday. It was by this man Dariush. Who has been banned in his country Iran for 27 years. The important thing is, this guy didn't come to Turkey to sing to Turks, the place was full of people from Iran, as if meeting in a secret place by word of mouth. They sung about freedom and cried after their country overtaken by Mollas. A moving scene, it was. An example of collaborative art, by who else but one of the forerunners of the ANSI scene, ICE. Lots to check out and think about the future uses of collaborative art. And more net.art your way with the help of Furtherfield. Innovative and inspirational stuff, involving code, linguistics and art!

title: Ah Cama-Sotz - 30 Siecles de Sommeil
content:
Normally, I'm not too much into dark ambient - industrial stuff as you might guess from the lack of mentions on this blog. However this song is an exception. Ah Cama-Sotz, one of the bigger names in the industrial scene has released a new album recently, and this is the opening track. Quite haunting and disturbing as you would except, this track is devoid of any rhythm. Occasional strings and a dominant eastern vibe took me to the slave markets of the past, and what better way to complete it with a strange old vocal sample from a possible Turkish folk song. Suitable for the soundtrack of an evil Arabian nights, with djinns and efreets and all that!.
Go to the official page of Ah Cama-Sotz

title: Instrumental Rock Special #2 - 5ive Style
content: Is this the greatest riff ever? Probably not.. but it's unstoppable in my head right now!. If you wanna catch the fever, join the club because it's been nearly 10 years since this album debuted on Sub Pop and it's still fresh as ever. Chicago's 5ive Style is a four piece which features Tortoise drummer John Herndon on drums and Bill Dolan on the guitars. The opening track of the album Deep Marsh has got an incredibly catchy guitar riff backed up nicely by tight uptempo drumwork from Herndon. A fusion of rock and funk in their own unique sound. If you like this track be sure to look for the album in bargain bins, it's worth it. Download 5ive Style - Deep Marsh Watch videos from Sub Pop

title: Izmar // Oxygenfad // netlabel releases!
content:
Izmar is a Dutch artist on Monotonik . Although it's nothing ground breaking, this is one of the best produced netlabel EPs I've ever listened. The album is generally world music influenced downtempo, full of lush sounds and sitars a la Thievery Corporation. What's striking is the completeness of the songs, they are not experimental tracks or sketched ideas (like some netlabel stuff) but fully grown songs with tiptop production both sound and arrangement wise.. hats off!
Download Izmar - Conscious
Also noteworthy is Oxygenfad's third release on the Postunder label. This 7 song EP clocks 19minutes and begins with a striking minimal piano piece, Bambino di vendetta , and continues with experimental noisy ambient sounds.
Download Oxygenfad - Dimension X3
And a few tips in the mp3blog direction. A few days ago I mentioned Luminescent Orchestrii on Comfort Music. Those two songs grew on me more and more so here's a re-mention. Their music is the bastard child of Balkan gypsies and Irish fiddlers, soundtrack to a pagan ritual, very uptempo and danceable (well for some people anyway!). The song Stranger is my favourite, laden with a such a nice vocal melody, get it! And while you're there don't forget to check the Safety Scissors post. I just can't recommend you this tune enough. It was on the Staedtizism 4 compilation from Berlin's ~Scape records, which is the home for all those nice artists like Pole and Jan Jelinek.
and read this hilarious thread on ILM and check this huge bootleg blog and comment if you have the time!

title: The Kung Fu Monkeys
content: Continuing the recent surge, i've decided to post from one of my fave albums. If there is one CD (apart from Slayer's Reign in Blood) that I wish was longer, it's The Kung Fu Monkeys' "School's out, Surf's up, Let's fall in Love" from 2000. KFM is the embodiment of bubblegum pop, they sound as if they are still living in a parody of 50s Pleasantville. Lyrics cover diverse (!) topics like hula hoops, summercamps, tv, vegetables, surfing and love; and they seem to be written for intellectual high-school nerds who go skating with their platonic loves. Well ok I know it sounds gay and all that, but it's so naive, cheerful and catchy you just have to listen to it, even if only as an ode to tv shows and cartoons you watched in the past. BTW they seem to be defunct now. Download The Kung Fu Monkeys - I've got a crush on you Download The Kung Fu Monkeys - Miss Manners Download The Kung Fu Monkeys - Roller skate Date

title: Dirt Bike Annie - Are you ready for the summer
content: After mentioning KFM and getting 2 comments! (whooo! we're rolling!) Decided to post another nice track in the same vein. This one directly goes to all boy scout-summer camp-people among us. 'No more pencils no more books, no more teacher's dirty looks, no more math or history, summer time will set us free' How naive!. I'm 12 again. Bubblegum pop-punk at its best. title: Yesterday's New Quintet - Wanda Vidal
content: Definitely incredible stuff from Madlib. He's probably my favourite jazzy leftfield hiphop producer. He hasn't disappointed me ever, not once. This is a track from his side project Yesterday's New Quintet's last offering Sound Directions : The Funky side of Life on his own Stones Throw label. "The Funky Side of Life" represents Madlib's first full length collaboration with session musicians – players whose tenures include Macy Gray, The Dap Kings, Antibalas, Breakestra and Connie Price and The Keystones – on horns, guitar and backup keyboards. Killer hook, killer old jazzy vibe. I can't stop pretending i'm wearing a hat and chain-smoking.. and very nice website featuring all his projects. title: Gem alert ! Peter B, - The Moon Camera
content: I hope you noticed the lack of posts for awhile, that was because my computer died. Was strolling through some old cds today, and I came upon this gem from Peter Blasser. It's pretty hard to define his music, very out-of-this world and personal. Strange spacy ambience, and very atonal melodies. However it's eerily mellow and listenable. Ok I lack the necessary adjectives to describe his music. I'm so sad to see only 9 listens to Peter B on last.fm! (and 48 here. ) (when is last.fm going to fix these.. ) The liner notes read, "I used Supercollider to create an ever changing texture, tied to the meter of a simple poem. As a result, the form of the piece is generative and through-composed.the vocal textures all imitate the digital gestures and glitches of the source material." Download The Moon Camera by Peter B.

title: Volapük - Polyglöt
content: Volapük is an avantgarde band, formed by French drummer and composer Guigou Chenevier in the early 90s with cellist Guillaume Saurel and clarinetist Michel Mandel. Their avantgarde sound is very accessible, and with the addition of ex-After Dinner violinist Takumi Fukushima, the band has created a masterful album. Pitchfork defined their sound as a mixture of folk, gypsy music and circus music which i truly agree, it's definitely a strange and unique melting pot of prog rock and jazz as well. Volapük is also primarily the name of a constructed language like esperanto. Edit : I'm just terribly in love with this Nusrat song, masterful vocals and melody.. if you liked the Lumiinari Orchestra and the Tin Hat Trio songs from a few days ago you should definitely check this out. Download Volapük - Nusrat Download Volapük - Sanza

title: Ni Hao! on Tzadik!
content:
I will forever thank Deerhoof for the surge of spazz rock around, because their success has encouraged lots of likeminded musicians everywhere. Ni Hao! is an all girl trio from Kansai (like Afrirampo), with this really odd line up of 2 basses and 1 drums. Their music has elements of distorted surf guitar, punk, spazz rock, contrapuntal canons, cartoon vocals, silly j-pop melodies in it. The attitude in the music is terrific and as strange as it may seem (well it seemed strange to me anyways) they're signed to Tzadik. These Japanese people, they really are living in a strange cartoonish world and I enjoy every bit.
Available on Boomkat here with more sample songs. Read Tzadik : Search and Destroy thread for best Tzadik album tips on I Love Music

title: Okkyung Lee // Jarboe // Rubin Steiner
content: Wooooo, a nice day for blogging ! . Four new tracks featured on undomondo. For the first time the songs are featured on a freeserver, called sendspace. I checked through many and settled on sendspace, they never delete the link as long as it gets downloads, they give you 1200mb, they have a nice upload progress bar and you don't have to wait to download.. too good to be true! Ok off we go with the first one. I'm pretty sure this would end on my top 10 songs for 2005. Avant jazz at its best a la Tzadik. Okkyung Lee is a Korean cellist and composer who's moved to Boston at age 18 to study at the Berklee College of Music and New England Conservatory, she then migrated to New York in 2000 and began to play with John Zorn, Jim O'Rourke, Christian Marclay, and many others. The album produced by Zorn himself and assisted with various instrumentalists and Ikue Mori on laptops is top class, and this song has a sensational melodic structure in a complex time signature. Available on Boomkat. Jarboe is a madwoman. She has worked in the past with the New York avantrock band Swans. This should definitely be the soundtrack for the torture session you're gonna give your victim in a few mins.. Very unhedonistic and dark, the track "sinner" is extremely agitating with a distorted vocal, chanting "Fuck your soul". Extreme stuff.. And last but not least, I wanna take you out of the darkness with a funny song by none other than the French electro downtempo - jazzy hiphop master Rubin Steiner. Saw him live once with his 3-piece orchestra and they are definitely a treat on stage.. This song features tens of European names in it, wanna check if you got your name in the list? title: Fat Freddy's Drop - Roady
content: Fat Freddy's Drop is a 7-piece band from NZ and what's striking is I felt that before I found about it. The music is similar to Salmonella Dub's sound and the line "do it for the love of music" popped the timeless Salmonella classic "Version" in my head. Their 2005 release has claimed a huge local and worldwide success, and although I haven't listened to it, this single gives me enough hints about it. Their digital dub groove sound is fresh, with great brass licks and vocals. Vocalist Joe Dukie is a familiar figure, he's the one who did the vocals on Recloose's incredible Dust track, which was featured here a few months ago. Roady has an uplifting and laidback mood at the same time, with a great chorus and a great bridge at 2:55. Very urban and accessible, the b-side of this single has a broken-beat house remix by the Nextmen that's equally good. Out on Sonar Kollektiv, so you know what to expect. Download Roady by Fat Freddy Read a review of their LP, Based on a True Story

title: Asa-Chang & Junray - Parlor
content:
I first heard about Asa-Chang & Junray with the song Hana a few years ago. This was a radically different music than the Western conception of music. Tabla was used like the Indian tabla masters, creating syllables that matched with Asa-Chang's singing, however the music and the lyrics were Japanese, a strange hybrid. It's so interesting that the Western and Eastern cultures have this radical difference between their worldviews, perhaps because of the differences in their language system or their music or the climate, I don't know. One thing I know is Hana was an epic song, with an irrational rhythmic structure (in Western musicology), vocals matching syllables created with tabla, over melancholic and cinematic strings. It wasn't easy listening, but it was rewarding for sure. It was a journey to an unknown territory, not marked by the rational western culture.. Now today I present you Parlor, a song more easily conceived, but surely with the trademark Asa-Chang & Junray sound; an incredible ancient Eastern motif on frantic tablawork. Guaranteed to take you to a trip to a past life in the Eastern hemisphere, where you could really understand what this music meant. And also thanks to the nice guys at Leaf, here is the video to Hana, which started it all for me. A must see!
Download Asa-Chang & Junray - Parlor Download Asa-Chang & Junray - Nigatsu Watch the video for Asa-Chang & Junray - Hana Buy Hana 12" here Read a review on BBC (also read the user comments)
Milkfactory review : As challenging a listening experience as it is, Jun Ray Song Chang is ultimately a beautiful and imaginative record, bringing an entire new dimension to anyone who has the curiosity to open their mind enough.

title: The joggers - Ziggurat Traffic
content:

Perhaps the song seems too overpowering compared to the rest of the album and if it was a more straightforward indie piece and if it had a voice it would yell something like "Dammit make me a video and make it half animation and half video art that will make Maximo Park cry." but alas! If you like your indie with excessive riffage, assymetrical stops and eastern influence, this is the one for you. The eastern piece (it feels odd to call something eastern since i am from the east myself) that the song is based on, sounds so familiar and well known but i can't put a name to it. maybe one of you can, huh? For the curious, I included a nice interview with the band members and don't worry: no "my girlfriend made me do it"s, no "i cut myself"s. Just enough to let you know about their view of music and some interesting stuff on the Portland scene.

title: Fedayi Pacha
content:
Fedayi Pacha has been on my tracklist for a few months, but the time to post about him has just come. I first heard about him on a French dub compilation featuring him and Zenzile among others. Then I got his album Dub Works, out on Hammerbass a French Label. The music is what you would expect from his name. Well sorry, most of our readers are from the US, so the meaning of Fedayi Pacha wouldn't ring a bell probably. Fedayi means something like a personal bodyguard that would go to death for you, and Pacha is well, a Pacha, something like a general in oriental countries. So to sum up, this is going to be an oriental dub album.. Fedayi Pacha is a French orientalist, interested in all kinds of Middle Eastern sounds. Should I suspect he is from Algerie or Morocco, I don't know, most of his interviews are in French, so I'm not sure of his descent. This album translates the powerful Middle Eastern motifs through electronic dub.. Ah, the sound of the desert and barren wastelands and nomad tents..

title: A Touch of Hip-hop
content:
Greetings to you all, my fellow Undo citizens. I've been soaked into hiphop nowadays and decided it was time to do a little dedicated corner. The hip-hop highlight of my recent playlists was Haiku d'etat. The triumverate, consisting of our legendary Aceyalone, Mikah 9 (from The Freestyle Fellowship) and Abstract Rude (from Abstract Tribe Unique) have their roles nicely played out: Aceyalone as "the poet", Mikah as "the jazz" and Abstract as "the soul". Spoken-word has got to have a certain poetic socio-political depth to it, but it doesn't always come in a such deeply soulful and jazzy package. Especially those in-between sax flows help a great deal of course. I haven't heard their newest album "Coup de Theatre", but if it's half as good as their self-titled year 2000 album, it's definitely worth a shot. As always, i don't want to trouble our precious html margins with excessive band statistics and invite you to get your informational nutrients from this nice interview.
Download Los Dangerous by Haiku D'Etat
Another loved one is none other than our good old friend Dj Vadim, Russia's sole pride in the Ninja Tune artist roster. His "children of the possibility"with his side project, One self, is among the smoothest hip hop i've heard this year. Here, we have this soft" in-between-styles" flow, which i definitely like about a hip hop release; nice soft grimy underlining with perfectly matching vocal numbers, soulful blues and even an occasional indian tap here and there. Yummy.

title: Jewish Twists of Solomon Schwartz
content:
After a small break, here we are with a new logo, and better colors (i hope).Todays post is a great one, inspired by a tag I saw on last.fm > songs you can listen to over 50 times in a row.. well, I'm pretty confident that I can listen to these songs at least 10 times before getting slightly bored. Solomon Schwartz has taken traditional jewish songs and made them into twist songs, in 1963 should I add. And were it not for the 2004 reissue, these gems would probably be lost. The opening track is the most wellknown Jewish song Hava Nagila. I'm pretty sure only one listen will be enough to first laugh out loud and then repeat the track for at least 3 times in a row. There are twelve songs on this album reissued on Solnze records and if you're a Jew you should definitely get this and surprise your elders at the Chanukah. I'm sure most of them will dance the twist despite their aching backs! Happy holidays to everyone!

Bobby Brown by Queen of Japan (Zappa cover) Bobby Brown by Frank Zappa White Horse by Queen of Japan

title: Winter Fiesta
content:
Greetings. I have heard from a reliable source, that the minimal techno gods wanted sacrifice so here i am with these two... Mersenne, has told me that Sao Paris reminded him of Agf/Delay. That is true but without the cold European attitude. Not that i'm against Europeans, really, I am a big fan of Europeans but this takes "down" out of downtempo. Not unlike the Brasilian reference in the name, the soft flat tones are tinted with a certain warmth, which is what you get if you are a French electronic musician with a Brasilian vocalist. Unlike many minimal downtempo releaseses, the album is not a whole matter of atmosphere which you can't differentiate one song from another. Every song is full of pretty much bull's eye personality, even fused with some broken beat every now and then. I actually asked for help whether to choose this song or that to post. Please admire their album movimento and give your regards to f comm for laying the chunky beats beside for a change and putting some great downtempo out there for us.
Sao Paris - Ria Sao Paris - Samba de Injustica Gustav is another story. It's a "she" by the way, don't let a moniker fool you. Switching from English to German to French, Gustav aka Eva Jantschitsch has so many stories to tell like her American patriot brother or One handed Mona who married Karl. You don't know what i'm talking about of course, but there is one way to figure it out since I am curious about the German lyrics and need someone to translate me. "Rettet Die Vale" is a lush, dusky, mysterious scrapbook of an album that "takes you away" again with our all so favoured switching between styles. I can't believe I said "takes you away" though, I thought I had buried that phrase years ago in some newspaper's weekend supplement. anyways, yay for the winter attitude.
Gustav - Linzserenade Gustav - One Handed Mona

title: Pierre Bastien - Noon
content: I've heard of Mr. Bastien's name on a multitude of mp3blogs, most notably on Radio Babylon. Although I'm not sure why I don't remember that his main source of music was his handmade mechanical robot orchestra. When I heard this track off his new album, I thought "hey another minimal electronica" record, although the sound wasn't very similar and it didn't feel like a Rephlex record. The feeling of the music was more similar to earlier minimalist artists like Glass or Reich and it sounded very futuristic, when the song faded into an eclectic Eastern brass solo after 4th minute, I decided to check out a bit on him. The story came to an end when I checked Mr. Bastien's site. He is a French multi instrumentalist composer, born in 1953, graduated from Sorbonne in 1977 and he has been making music, art and installations with his mechanical orchestra since then.. ! Aquarius records says "Why form a band, when you can construct robots and machines to play all the instruments? Why actually play the piano, or the guitar, or the drums, when you can construct an elaborate set of pulleys and levers and gears and axles that will play them for you?" That's the perfect explanation for Mr. Bastien. This is not electronic, this is indeed mechanical music and it's minimal tone and subtle melodies are composed so well that you will be amazed to see how much most of the young electronica artists lack as opposed to this middle-aged master. Then you think about how he has made those machines .. and the mind boggles.. First download Noon by Pierre Bastien. then head over here for an interview with this amazing personality, who is a wealth of knowledge and intellect.. and then finally go buy the album @ Boomkat Alternatively you could head to his site and download more tracks by him; like Damn Mad and Avid Diva PS: Discovered an old but essential blog post on the ever so deep WFMU blog, a post about mechanized music composers in which you could discover 10+ other mechanical musicians including Conlon Nancarrow (who really deserves a stand alone post one day) and Remko Scha, and also download one more track by Pierre Bastien.

title: Top artists in 2005
content: Well my top albums list doesn't resemble my top artists of the year, so I thought I should add a little thanks list for my preferred musicians this year. no.1 is Deerhoof : I can't tell you how much I love Deerhoof, I didn't add their album to the list, not that it wasn't good but it wasn't all good.. but I should have added it to runners up at least, my bad.. so here is where I pay my dues.. Deerhoof is the best band in the world right now!. Ok there I said it ! (mov) - My pal foot foot - Panda Panda Panda Live - Flower no.2 is Madlib : Madlib has taken production to another level; he has this magic chemical material (THC? :) ) that he adds to every song he does, whether he's Quasimoto or one half of Madvillain, or Yesterday's New Quintet or Beat Konducta.. He's making these short caricatures of moments and God bless him, he's great!. Just watch the video to see how much love this brother gives/deserves. (mov) - The Payback no.3 is MF Doom : MF Doom is Madlib's kooky partner in crime. He might be obsessed with cartoons, but who isn't. He's a terrific MC and although I might be late to discover him, I think I've been a worthy fan this year. (mov) no.4 is Devendra Banhart : I didn't like Devendra's 2005 album that much, It has some lovely songs yeah, but it isn't top notch as an album. However I think he's a terrific artist with an unbelievable songwriting ability and some of the best songs I listened to in 2005 belong to him. A sight to behold - At the hop no.5 is John Zorn : Uncle John is here not because of his musicianship, but because of Tzadik. He still has the best vision and he's released lots of diverse stuff this year and helped me find tons of nice stuff. Hope you never get old, man! So the overall keyword of this year is "attitude". I'm terribly bored of musicians / djs who see their productions as sacred, labels / image makers who think image is everything, artists who spend millions on their homes and clothes, and generally people who believe in the lie that they're going to be the next big thing and act like that. Wake up guys. Rock stars are so 90s. Thanks to all artists who release stuff on independent labels, who put free mp3s on their sites, who drink a beer or smoke a joint after the show with their fans, who reply emails personally and who are in this biz not to make money but to have fun and make life bearable. Next year will be much much better!

title: Silver Jews
content:
I don't know why I like southern rock/country. I've never been to the US, and I don't have anything common with the southern uhh "ideals", but I can't stop my feet when I listen to the banjo or the fiddle!. Can I be saved? Anyways Mr. David Berman here is an indie rock icon who has survived a suicide attempt a few years ago, and on this album he gets assisted by lots of his old friends like Stephen Malkmus of Pavement. He is surely one of those old poet guys who really has the lyrical ability to write songs properly. This song is a proof to that as he's made a hilarious protest/satiric anthem from the eyes of a pony. The song is pretty uptempo and packed with lyrics, it's a frenzy of basic guitars with a huge punk attitude. Can we say Southern Rock is the new Punk? nah I'm just kidding, just get the song and enjoy.

title: Gerry Hemingway Quartet - Rallier
content:
I know I have been lacking on the avantjazz/freejazz front for some time although I've been listening to a few great albums I've picked up recently. And surprise they are not on Tzadik this time! :) Gerry Hemingway Quartet's latest album The Whimbler is on the Portuguese Clean Feed label that focus on creative jazz. Mr. Hemingway is a drummer and his Quartet has been around since 1977, although with changing musicians throughout time. The music is centered around his rhythmic grooves and freestyling although you can hear some incredible synchronization with the brass section throughout the album. The thing with freejazz is, it's rewarding music although not at the first listen like easier music. You just have to stick through the song to see the beauty, because most of the time, the untrained listener gets bored after a few seconds of undecipherable noise and strange time signatures. Don't do that ! listen to this track at least for a minute and get a taste of this magnificent freebop tune..

title: Safety Scissors - Tainted Lunch
content:
Greetings,I've been having trouble finding review-worthwhile music lately. I don't know why, I just hope that i haven't become snobbish to the extent of not liking anything anymore. Let's just cut the crap by saying music can be tiring sometimes and start talking about the owner of these quotes:
"Anonymity is much more interesting. It's silly when people say they are an artist or a musician. They're just trying to cover up for something else that they don't have a girlfriend or smell bad or suffer from alcoholism."
Unfortunately for Matthew Patterson Curry or Safety Scissors as we know him, it's hard to remain anonymous when you're making music like that. He likes to eat ice cream, ride his bicycle and make minimal techno that shines through a gazillion of the same old clickclacky releases. His earlier releases hadn't really caught my attention but he got me some time before with his slanty, lighthearted style in "Amnesia" which i guess has become a pretty familiar song in it's scene by now. His matchingly pretty album "Tainted Lunch" has not only freshened his image but also his label ~scape's image by adding new warmth to the label's cold german attitude (minding the fact that the album was mixed by Vladislav Delay). Call it micro-house, minimal-techno or the newly acquired "hiccup-funk", it's tasteful no matter what you call it. MP3s removed after contact from label. Buy the album from Boomkat.

title: Andrew Pekler - Strings and Feedback
content:
Andrew Pekler's latest offering on Staubgold is a 10 piece album that doesn't sound like his previous stuff on ~Scape. (I was going to post an mp3 from his previous album, but remembered just in time that it was on ~Scape and I don't want anymore trouble with them so everyone go back to your Station to Station CD if you wanna remember how his sound was!).This album is mostly devoid of any beats, but it has a slew of slow growing, piano and string feedbacks, stutters and tonal ambience that form their own rhythm. It's a very calm album, and you have to be patient and listen to the tracks a few times to get the feeling right. The samples are mostly decomposed from Morton Feldman's work in the 1950s. He's used grain delays and created out of this world poetic sequences with great attention. Tense at times, like 50s space movies, the soundscapes he's created are barren and minimalistic, and the songs are mostly short. I highly recommend this album (especially with headphones because there's so much detail here that would go unnoticed without them.) and I think it might end up in my top of 2006 list too!

title: Cassetteboy - Dead Horse & more
content:
The funniest guys in UK are back! Don't you just love the politically incorrect UK guerilla humour? Don't you love the accent?? I sure do, and I've laughed countless times listening to this tape Dead Horse, and their previous bootleg with DJ Rubbish - Inside a whale's cock!. content:
Hi all, please excuse our absence for the last 3 weeks!

Well I'm sure I've proven I'm not so quick when it comes to doing shit. It took me 3 weeks to import the data from blogger and add plugins to wp, along with other things of course.. (note that i'm just a css/php novice as well :/) . I would have made some posts in the meantime, had blogger stopped acting weird and let me post, but after the import blogger stopped version (no idea why)..

Anyways here's v2.0? of undomondo, with a better layout, archives, tags, neater links and instant reblog of other mp3blogs on the sidebar.... I have listened to some great music in the meantime, and now I shall begin with one of them!

Microfilm is an instrumental rock band from France and has been at the top of my playlist constantly for the last few weeks. They've made a powerful album mostly based on tight drum and guitar work. Although there are no vocals, there are audio snippets from movies (I am a sucker for ephemeral audio from radio/cinema) which fit the music very well. The album certainly has a black and white science movie feel to it. Maybe that's because of the cover work, or their website, I'm not quite sure, but listen to Secret Camera and tell me you didn't feel it!

You will notice that this band has no bells and whistles in their sound, but IMHO that's because they don't need it. These guys have cut the crap and delivered an emotional (but not EMO emotional, doh) yet sincere album. I must admit I've listened to some songs on repeat more than once and I think they do deserve to be heard by a greater audience.

title: Kobol - Broken Ebony
content:
Greetings from sunny Mexico. Here are some debut delicacies by our new Mexican friends Kobol. The album Broken Ebony is released by Tijuana label Static Discos,which also features Fax and our dark prince of avant-strings, Murcof.
"A jazz album for tweekheads and an electronic album for jazzheads" says the catalogue description and i couldn't agree more.
Kobol duo Nashio Chavez and Argel Medina have captured quite a neat sound; a nice combination of various jazzy moves (from laidback to roughly asymmetrical) with pausy beats and digital processing and although there are lots of contrasting elements in the music, the experimental side, although strong, is kept well controlled under the in-between-songs-flow. This makes the album quite a head-to-toe listening experience. I like these kinds of albums especially when doing long and concentrated work. Muy bien amigos, keep up the good work.

title: Heavy Deviance
content:
Heavy Deviance is a soulful, deep house duo from UK. If you like stuff like The Rurals (which you should!) you'd be familiar with the laidback, rhodesy UK house sound.. well add a bit of electro and downtempo beats to it and you get a solid urban album from the fresh Pure-Mint label. I selected 2 songs from the album, yet it was a close call.. "Day by Day" is a moody song with jazzy chords from a rhodes, and great vocals by Lauren Surridge. It's got a 2/4 shuffle rhythm, something that's highly unlikely to be on an album of this type, I guess they have some German influence in them as well! :) Anyways, what I should probably add is, although I have used many catch phrases like downtempo, electro and deep house, Heavy Deviance is hard to categorise. They have an eclectic sound and many ideas for songs for variance. The second track is "Safe + Warm" which is a 90-100BPM veeeery laidback disco track, with great & sexy vocals male vocals . I would say this is a definite hit that would rock your dancefloor (if you play around those BPMs of course!) or your sofa! Well at least you can get the album and play this track to your ex-gf tomorrow!
"Now I know that you're a heart headed woman, but I wanna keep you safe and warm // Let's start again tomorrow, baby let me please prove you wrong. // Gimme one more chance!"

title: Bruce Haack - Captain Entropy
content:
This was undoubtedly the happiest find i had for months. Theatrical (almost like a BBC drama) spoken-word nature documentaries all along tinny claviers, bluegrass melodies, soulful choruses and all sounding like it's coming from your grandpa's phonograph... While at first i thought Bruce Haack was some wacky minimal musician's moniker and this album was his idea of a 70's joke, it really turned out to be an authentic electronic piece from '73. Haack (1931-1988), had been building his own electronic instruments since the 60s. He believed in the power of music to communicate with people, especially children and he produced educational records for kids, educational spoken word over electronic music, like Captain Entropy. Some of the lyrics are pretty funny and clever, not in the least "i can spell my own name" childish. I'll definitely be hearing more from him. There is even a movie about him which has become an official selection in many independent festivals with appearances by artist including Gary Moore! and Mouse on Mars.
More info on Haack (and some other info about "The definitive Compilation", by Bruce Haack, Esther Nelson & Dimension 5.) on the Emperor Norton site.

title: Yid Vicious - The Seventh Schlemiel
content:
Hailing from Wisconsin, this funny klezmer band has a great name that instantly knocked me up. A band with this name would surely have a great attitude I thought not taking themselves too seriously at all. Boy was I right!. This is a great CD, especially if you have a previous notion of Balkan brass music and klezmer (well, I know most people wouldn't count themselves as a klezmer fan) but don't dismiss them if you don't. Because this album can easily transfer the cheerfulness of the bar mitzvahs or the outdoor weddings to your houses (at some time including the vision of the happy jews dancing around your living room..). It's easy for me to sympathise with klezmer because the music / culture is blended with the Slavic and the Turkish cultures too, and if you've ever been to the East of Europe, or watched a movie, you would surely feel the vibe. These vicious guys add up to a total of 7 and they play everything from clarinets to saxophones, and from fiddle to mandolin. This is their 3rd album and it's really hard to stop listening to their uptempo songs and go listen something else. I had a tie between 3 songs and had forced myself to choose 2, well I still mourn for the song I haven't chosen, I wish all you guys would buy this album and listen to it .. or you could go down to where the band is playing if you're around Madison, WI and tell the band you wish to listen to "Tsiganeshti". PS : Right after I finished this up, I found a link on CD Baby, that has a 2 minute preview for all songs..
